newsitem.title: EGYPT: Kuwait says no question of U.S. crossing to Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait says no question of U.S. crossing to Iraq.

text.p: Kuwait said on Sunday there was no question of U.S. land forces crossing into Iraq from Kuwaiti territory.
Kuwaiti Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Jaber al-Sabah told reporters in the Egyptian city of Alexandria that Kuwait, like other Gulf states, merely had U.S. planes at its air bases.
Asked if Kuwait agreed to let U.S. forces attack Iraq from its territory, he said:
"There is no passage for land forces, but there are air forces at Kuwaiti bases and this is not something new and they are also present in other states in the Gulf," he said.

Sheikh Sabah was speaking after a meeting with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak. He said he had given Mubarak messages from the Emir of Kuwait, Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah, and from the Crown Prince, Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah.
He also explained to Mubarak the measures Kuwait has taken in the crisis between Iraq and the United States.
